metadata.title: Survey of Adult Skills 2023 Technical Report (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This chapter is a technical documentation of PIAAC Cycle 2 background questionnaire (BQ) development, validation, and translation/adaptation processes, rather than an empirical analysis estimating proficiency outcomes. It describes how the BQ is administered (CAPI on tablet, routing, timing, interviewer instructions, help buttons, and consistency checks) and how field trial (FT) data were used to evaluate item functioning, construct validity, and questionnaire length. Because the chapter does not present an analytic model for student-level achievement outcomes, it does not specify whether complex survey weights (e.g., final person weights) or replicate weights were applied in estimation. For users of PIAAC microdata, the standard approach is to apply the PIAAC sampling weights and replicate-weight variance estimation when producing population-representative estimates and standard errors; however, this chapter itself focuses on instrument quality and comparability checks rather than weighted outcome estimation.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values (PVs) are not applicable here because the chapter does not estimate cognitive achievement outcomes (literacy, numeracy, APS) using PV-based scoring; instead, it documents questionnaire development, translation/adaptation, and validation of BQ items/scales using FT and MS design checks. Missing-data handling is also not reported as an estimation strategy for PV-based models; the chapter discusses item non-response patterns and routing/quality checks, but does not specify a formal missing-data method (e.g., listwise deletion or multiple imputation) for an analytic model.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The chapter reports multiple development/validation activities rather than a single analytic sample. For the mixed-method online pretest, it targeted approximately 500 respondents per country (France, Germany, Japan, Poland, United States) drawn from online access panels with quotas by age (16–30, 31–50, 51–65), education (low/medium/high), and sex, and required respondents to be employed or self-employed with an expected 80% having participated in at least one training event; some quota targets were relaxed due to fieldwork challenges. For FT BQ validation analyses, international FT analyses used PIAAC Cycle 2 FT data collected in 2021; for most analyses, only completed interviews and partial completes were included, while for item functioning, routing checks, multi-item scales in Section K, multivariate analyses, and timing analyses, only completed cases were included (break-offs excluded to avoid distortions in missing-data computations and BQ length). For timing analyses, extreme response times were capped (response times exceeding four times the country median) and interviews with total BQ response time under 10 minutes were treated as unrealistic; Croatia (HRV) was excluded from some international averages due to extremely short timing.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD technical report chapter documents how the PIAAC Cycle 2 background questionnaire (BQ) was developed, translated/adapted, and validated using field trial (FT) and pretest evidence. It explains the conceptual framework linking BQ content to PIAAC policy questions, the BQ structure (11 sections including social and emotional skills), and the operational design features that support comparability (routing, interviewer instructions, help buttons, and consistency checks). For validation, it reports FT-based checks of questionnaire length and timing (including outlier capping and unrealistic short-interview exclusion), item non-response and distributional plausibility, routing correctness, and multi-item scale functioning (including IRT/WLE-based scaling for skill-use scales and psychometric evaluation for Big Five short forms). It also describes translation/adaptation governance (decentralised national centres with consortium linguistic quality assurance, double translation and reconciliation, and verification workflows). The chapter’s results are primarily instrument-quality and comparability decisions (e.g., which items to drop or revise for the main study), rather than predictive modeling of adult proficiency.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is a technical documentation chapter focused on questionnaire development, translation/adaptation, and validation procedures for PIAAC Cycle 2, not an empirical predictive/causal study with a defined ML target variable and reported model performance. As a result, there is no student-level ML model to extract (ml_techniques is empty), no PV-based outcome modeling (plausible values are not applicable), and no main_findings rows are produced because the chapter’s outputs are instrument design recommendations and quality-check results rather than predictive effects.
